title: Kitchen and Garden
premise: Silas Eastwick has spent ten years ghostwriting the memoirs of celebrity chef Margot Vance while secretly answering fan letters addressed to Margot — including a decade-long correspondence with a gardener named Wren who believes she knows him. When Wren moves into the cottage next door to his island home, hired to restore the inn's kitchen garden, Silas must decide whether to confess his deception or keep the lie alive to protect Margot's final book deal. As Wren's warmth draws his lonely island community into something like family, and Margot's publisher demands a tell-all that would betray everyone Silas loves, loyalty and truth pull him apart. He confesses at the dock as the last ferry of the season idles; Wren stays, and together they plant the inn's spring garden — his first honest words growing beside hers.
about_author: Ansel Reyes is the pen name of a former line cook turned novelist who spent six years writing other people's stories before claiming one of his own. He lives on a cold coast with a stubborn herb garden and a deep belief that kitchens are where people tell the truth.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Margins
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. On his island cottage, Silas finishes ghosting chapter forty of Margot Vance's memoir and answers a fan letter in her voice — the routine that has defined his decade. The beat: competent loneliness, a man fluent in everyone's voice but his own.

chapters.title: A Crate of Seedlings
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. A moving truck arrives next door; Wren Calloway, the gardener whose letters he's answered for ten years, steps out to restore the inn's kitchen garden. He recognizes her instantly; she doesn't know his face. The beat: panic braided with longing.

chapters.title: Margot's Deadline
chapters.summary: Margot's POV, via phone call. Margot, ill and tired of her own myth, pushes Silas to include the real story of her rise — which means exposing the letters, the ghost, and the people she's used. The beat: guilt arriving on schedule.

chapters.title: Compost and Small Talk
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren settles in, charmed by her taciturn neighbor who seems oddly fluent in her favorite topics. She wonders why the island feels like somewhere she's already grieved. The beat: belonging knocking politely.

chapters.title: The Letter She Kept
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren shows Silas a worn letter 'Margot' wrote during her worst winter — the one that kept her alive. Silas, its actual author, can barely breathe. The beat: the weight of a kindness that has become a debt.

chapters.title: Sunday Supper
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Wren cooks for the inn's ragtag regulars — the ferry captain, the retired postmistress, the teenage dishwasher — and Silas is folded in without being asked. The beat: found family forming before his eyes, terrifying in its ease.

chapters.title: What Margot Wants
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Margot arrives unannounced, glamorous and frail, and insists Silas keep Wren close: 'The gardener's good material.' Silas realizes he's a prop in someone else's story again. The beat: loyalty curdling into complicity.

chapters.title: Frost Warning
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren and Silas save the seedlings from a late frost through the night, hands brushing, walls lowering. She tells him why she came to the island: to thank Margot in person, and to find whoever wrote that letter. The beat: intimacy and encroaching exposure.

chapters.title: Drafts and Confidences
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Margot's publisher demands the tell-all chapter — names, letters, the truth about the ghostwritten fan mail — or the book dies. Silas stalls, lying to Margot, to Wren, to himself. The beat: the lie requiring more lies.

chapters.title: The Inn's Empty Chairs
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren learns the inn will close in spring unless the garden revival draws visitors; she throws herself into planning a harvest festival, and the islanders rally. The beat: hope as collective labor, Silas at the edge of the circle.

chapters.title: Margot and the Mirror
chapters.summary: Margot's POV. Margot watches Wren and Silas together and recognizes the love she traded away for the myth. She wavers between protecting her legacy and setting them free. The beat: the rival as a wounded human.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. At the festival planning, Silas nearly tells Wren the truth; instead he gives her a gift — a letter he writes as himself for the first time in a decade, unsigned. The beat: courage in the wrong currency.

chapters.title: The Publisher's Call
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The publisher threatens to hire another ghost and publish the letters with or without Silas's cooperation. Margot's health fails; she asks Silas to finish the book 'honestly.' He hears it as permission to confess. The beat: doors opening and closing at once.

chapters.title: What Wren Saw
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren finds Silas's manuscript pages in the cottage — the memoir draft, and within it, phrasing she knows by heart from the letters. She says nothing, testing the sentence against her memory all night. The beat: the ground shifting.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Greenhouse
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren asks Silas directly who wrote the letters. He lies to her face — protecting Margot's book deal, he tells himself. She walks away, and the island's warmth seems to walk away with her. The beat: the cost of a second lie.

chapters.title: Margot's Last Chapter
chapters.summary: Margot's POV. Margot, hospitalized on the mainland, records a voice memo releasing Silas from every promise: 'Tell her. The book can be about the truth or it can be about me, not both.' The beat: absolution arriving late but arriving.

chapters.title: The Ferry Schedule
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas learns the last ferry of the season departs in three days; Wren has booked a ticket, her trust spent, her purpose here finished. The beat: a clock finally loud enough.

chapters.title: Rehearsed for a Decade
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas writes and burns three drafts of the truth, then does the braver thing: he goes to Wren with no script at all and tells her everything — the letters, the ghostwriting, the lie, the sentence he's rehearsed for ten years. The beat: confession as release, not absolution.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren stands at the dock with her ticket as Silas's words settle. She boards — then steps off before the gangway lifts, telling him the letters were never Margot's gift to her; they were his. The beat: forgiveness as a choice, not a feeling.

chapters.title: Margot's Truth
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The memoir publishes with Silas's name beside Margot's and the letters' true authorship disclosed. Margot, reading the galleys in her hospital bed, calls it 'the only chapter I didn't lie in.' The beat: truth costing something and giving back more.

chapters.title: First Frost, Last Planting
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren and Silas plant garlic and tulip bulbs in the inn's garden for spring, the islanders hauling mulch and arguing about compost like family. The inn's future is still uncertain, but no one is alone in it. The beat: belonging chosen daily.

chapters.title: The Sentence, Said
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. On the morning the first ferry of the new season arrives, Silas says the rehearsed sentence plainly — that he loves her, has loved her through every letter — and Wren answers with a sentence of her own. The beat: quiet, earned joy; the story closing on an open gate.
